claims.claim: Situational Awareness LP sold its entire public equity book, longs and shorts, to Citadel in a single block around the 30 July 2026 US open, after margin calls from Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Bank of America.

Situational Awareness LP (CIK 0002045724) has filed six consecutive 13F-HRs; the Q1 2026 filing, filed 18 May 2026, reported $13,676,657 thousand across 42 holdings, up from $254,813 thousand across 6 holdings at Q4 2024.
Roughly $8.46 billion, or 62%, of the Q1 2026 13F value was put-option exposure measured at underlying value, chiefly SMH, NVDA, ORCL and AVGO puts, leaving disclosed long equity near $5.2 billion.

Reported start-of-July fund size ranges from ~$45 billion (CNBC, single anonymous source) to $20-24 billion (WSJ, Faber), with the public equity book put at ~$16 billion by the FT and post-sale assets near $10 billion.
The fund returned +439% net in the first half of 2026, a figure sourced solely to a 24 July 2026 investor letter reviewed by the Financial Times.

The circulating 'up 2,000% in 2025' figure is arithmetically inconsistent with the WSJ's June 2026 reporting of >1,000% since inception and ~270% in 2026 through May, which together imply a 2025 calendar return closer to +200%.

Regulation T caps initial margin at 50%, permitting only 2x long exposure; FINRA Rule 4210(c) sets maintenance at 25% of long market value and 30% of short, so a 4x gross book sits at the maintenance floor with no buffer at inception.

At 4x gross leverage split 2.6x long and 1.4x short, a 35% long decline combined with a 10% adverse move in the shorts exhausts 105% of equity; the wipeout threshold on the longs alone is roughly a 33% decline.

July 2026 peak-to-trough declines from the 30 June close to the 29 July trough close reached -55.3% for SanDisk, -50.1% for SK hynix, -46.3% for Nebius, -45.9% for Bloom Energy, -38.9% for CoreWeave and -36.0% for Micron.

The S&P 500 was roughly flat in July 2026 at -0.7% month-to-date while SOXX fell 21.3% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 28.6% from its 22 June peak, establishing the drawdown as idiosyncratic rather than market beta.

On 30 July 2026, after the liquidation was reported, the affected names rebounded 18-31% in a single session -- IREN +30.5%, Nebius +27.1%, Bloom Energy +26.5%, SanDisk +26.0%, CoreWeave +21.5% -- against SOXX +8.5% and SPY +1.7%.

Bloom Energy reported record Q2 2026 results on 28 July 2026 -- revenue $1,065.4M, +165.5% year over year, with full-year guidance raised -- and the stock still fell to its July low the following session.
UBS's AI-capex basket trailed its AI-disruption-risk basket by a record 42 percentage points in July 2026.
Goldman Sachs' US high-beta momentum basket fell roughly 37% in July 2026, its worst month in the series' history back to 1999, and the Morgan Stanley Momentum TMT Index fell 53.5%.

Adobe rose 20.9% in July 2026 without reporting earnings, after a Morgan Stanley downgrade to Underweight on 21 July took its price target to $240; Workday rose 29.2%, Salesforce 15.4% and ServiceNow 10.9% over the same month.

Goldman Sachs prime brokerage recorded information technology as the most net-sold US sector for a fourth consecutive week in the week to 3 July 2026, and separately reported hedge funds cutting US tech exposure roughly 10% over eight weeks, the largest sector retreat in the series' history.

Asia fundamental long/short hedge funds tracked by Goldman fell 18.6% month-to-date through 28 July 2026 after peaking at +40% year-to-date on 22 July, with the largest five-day cumulative de-grossing on Goldman's record.
Five-year CDS on AI-levered borrowers widened sharply into late July 2026, with CoreWeave near 855bp and Oracle near 215bp against roughly 145bp at the end of 2023.

Bloomberg reported on 1 July 2026 that Meta was preparing to rent out excess AI compute under an internal programme called Meta Compute; semiconductor and neocloud equities fell sharply that session, with SOX down 6.3%.
Archegos Capital Management grew from ~$1.5B of capital and $10B of exposure in March 2020 to more than $36B of capital and $160B of exposure at peak, roughly 4.4x gross leverage.
Archegos produced more than $10 billion of counterparty losses, disclosed within one business day: Credit Suisse ~$5.5B, Nomura $2.85B, Morgan Stanley $911M, UBS ~$861M, MUFG ~$300M.
No prime broker has disclosed any loss arising from the Situational Awareness liquidation as of 31 July 2026, and no fraud, misrepresentation or manipulation has been alleged against the fund.
Bill Hwang was convicted on ten counts in July 2024 and sentenced to 18 years in November 2024 for deliberately misleading counterparties about Archegos's exposure, concentration and liquidity.
The SEC formally withdrew proposed Rule 10B-1, the security-based swap position disclosure rule written in direct response to Archegos, in June 2025, leaving the swap-opacity gap open.

Citadel has absorbed distressed books before: Amaranth's energy portfolio in September 2006 with a reported concession near $1.85-2.15 billion at roughly 50 cents on the dollar, and Sowood's credit book in July 2007, on which it is reported to have made large profits.
The price and discount at which Citadel acquired the Situational Awareness book have not been disclosed by any party.

Aschenbrenner's June 2024 essay forecast a ladder of ~1M GPUs, tens of billions of dollars and ~1GW for a 2026 cluster, ~10GW by 2028 and ~100GW by 2030, with AI reaching roughly 5% of US electricity production by 2026 and 20% by 2028.

METR's measured 50% task-completion time horizon rose from 3.99 minutes for GPT-4 in March 2023 to 718.8 minutes for Claude Opus 4.6 in February 2026 and 1,044.8 minutes for an April 2026 Claude preview, with the 2023-onward doubling time at roughly 129 days rather than the originally reported seven months.

METR states that measurements above 16 hours are unreliable with its current task suite, and its Frontier Risk Report found at least 16% of successful runs on tasks over eight hours were illegitimate on review.

Big-four hyperscaler 2026 capital expenditure guidance as of late July 2026 totals roughly $720-745 billion -- Amazon ~$220B, Alphabet $195-205B, Microsoft ~$175B, Meta $130-145B -- against roughly $382 billion in 2025.

Every one of the big four hyperscalers raised or held 2026 capex guidance in the last week of July 2026; Microsoft's apparent $15 billion reduction was an accounting reclassification following an extension of datacenter useful life from 15 to 25 years.

Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion in Q2 2026, its first negative quarter as a public company, while raising 2026 capex guidance and guiding that free cash flow will remain under pressure.
LBNL's 2025 update put US datacenters at 192 TWh, or 4.7% of US electricity consumption, in 2024, and projects 649 TWh or 11.8% by 2030 in its reference case, with a full range of 9.5-15.3%.
US net electricity generation grew 2.8% in 2025 to 4,430 billion kWh, and EIA cut its 2026 growth forecast in December 2025 explicitly because large loads had not materialised as expected.
As of April 2026 only about 0.3 GW of the 9-plus GW of planned OpenAI Stargate US capacity was energized, with six of seven sites at zero.

LBNL's Queued Up 2026 edition reports a median interconnection-request-to-commercial-operation duration of over five years for projects built in 2025, with only 13% of 2000-2020 capacity reaching commercial operation and 75% withdrawn.

Realized all-in cost per gigawatt of AI datacenter capacity runs roughly $35-40 billion, three to four times the roughly $10 billion per gigawatt implied by Aschenbrenner's 2026 rung, so the dollar milestones arrive far earlier than the power milestones.

Anthropic's post-money valuation ladder ran $4.6B (Series C, May 2023), $18.4B (Series D, Dec 2023), $61.5B (Series E, March 2025), $183B (Series F, Sept 2025), $380B (Series G, Feb 2026) and $965B (Series H, 28 May 2026, $65B raised).
Situational Awareness LP is named by Anthropic itself as a participating investor in the Series H round.
The ~$5 billion Anthropic mark reported on 30 July 2026 references a primary round priced on 28 May 2026, a 63-day staleness gap that by construction excludes July's public-market repricing.
Anthropic secondaries were reported trading at an implied $1.2 trillion in early-to-mid July 2026, a roughly 24% premium to the $965 billion primary round, inverting the usual illiquidity discount.
No public secondary-market price observation for Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI or SpaceX exists for the 20-30 July 2026 selloff window; the latest located print is dated 13 July 2026.

ASC 820-10-35-24C requires valuation techniques to be calibrated so they reflect observable market data at the measurement date; there is no accounting exemption permitting a Level 3 holding to be frozen at the last round price.

NAV lending against fund portfolios reached a record $23 billion across 38 KBRA-rated transactions in 2025, but 84% of surveyed loans carried loan-to-value ratios of 20% or lower, versus 50%-plus advance rates typical on listed equity.

Fundrise Innovation Fund (VCX) reported an SEC-filed NAV of $18.97 per share as of 31 March 2026 with Anthropic marked at a $350 billion valuation, while its market premium to NAV compressed from roughly 356% in June 2026 to roughly 202% in late July 2026.

Destiny Tech100 (DXYZ), which holds Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX, closed at $23.50 on 30 July 2026 against a 52-week high of $72.87, with its last publicly reported NAV of $19.97 per share struck on 31 December 2025.
Tiger Global's hedge fund fell 52% in 2022 and wrote down its venture private marks by about 33% across that year, establishing that private marks do move but with a two-to-four-quarter lag.

Liquidating the public book roughly doubles the Anthropic stake's share of fund NAV, from about 25% of a ~$20 billion fund to about 50% of a ~$10 billion residual, with no change in the private asset itself.
Hedge funds made roughly $24 billion shorting software stocks in the first weeks of 2026 and increased the position, making it the most crowded and most profitable short of the first half.

A single Wall Street Journal headline dated 31 July 2026 reports the fund down 67% in July; compounded against the reported +439% first half it would imply the fund is still positive year to date, but no outlet has published a post-unwind year-to-date or since-inception return.

SK hynix listed ADRs on Nasdaq in July 2026 in a roughly $26.5 billion offering, with newly issued underlying common shares additionally listed on KOSPI on 29 July Korea time, coinciding with the trough of the Korean leveraged unwind.

Ken Griffin said publicly at Davos in January 2026 that AI is hype -- 'How else are you getting people to write 500 billion dollars worth of checks?' -- while separately calling the technology real, a posture consistent with buying a discount rather than a thesis.
